Its appearance can be varied, such as being covered in leaves or featuring a crop farm nearby. The loot inside the chests can have explorer maps for various structures, such as other abandoned camps, trial chambers, and ancient cities.

entities.blurb: An ancient city is a palatial structure found in deep dark biomes at Y=-51, that harbors chests containing items, such as disc fragments, armor trims, and echo shards, that cannot be found anywhere else. It is also one of the only two places where sculk sensors can be found.
entities.name: Ancient City

entities.blurb: Bastion remnants, also simply referred to as bastions, are large, castle-like generated structures found in the Nether in all of the biomes except basalt deltas. They generate in four distinct variants, each with a unique structure and set of loot. Piglins and piglin brutes spawn in these structures on generation, and hoglins may also spawn on generation in the bridge and hoglin stables variants. Bastion remnants are the only place to find gilded blackstone, the Pigstep music disc, the snout banner pattern and armor trim, monster spawners which spawn magma cubes, and the netherite upgrade smithing template.
entities.name: Bastion Remnant

entities.blurb: A buried treasure is a naturally generated structure that consists of a buried loot chest. The chest is buried primarily in beaches, and rarely in the ocean floor. Buried treasures are the only source of the heart of the sea, which can be used to craft a conduit. Buried treasures can be located using explorer maps.
entities.name: Buried Treasure

entities.blurb: A desert pyramid or desert temple is an uncommon above ground structure found in desert biomes built mostly of sandstone and terracotta. The desert pyramid contains four loot chests hidden under the floor in the center, which are protected by a TNT trap, and a secret buried room to the side where archaeology can be performed by brushing the generated suspicious sand with a brush.
entities.name: Desert Pyramid

entities.blurb: End cities are tall structures found on the outer islands of the End. They are inhabited by shulkers and hold valuable loot, including enchanted iron and diamond tools, weapons, and armor. End ships, found in some End cities, are the only place where elytra and dragon heads can be obtained.
entities.name: End City

entities.blurb: A Nether fortress is an uncommon large structure made of Nether bricks found in the Nether, consisting of bridges, corridors, and towers. Nether fortresses are the only place where wither skeletons and blazes spawn. They also contain Nether wart.
entities.name: Nether Fortress

entities.blurb: An igloo is an uncommon structure generated in snowy taigas, snowy plains, or snowy slopes and built mainly of snow blocks. Some igloos contain hidden labs under the carpet, which serve as a tutorial for curing a zombie villager.
entities.name: Igloo

entities.blurb: A jungle pyramid, also known as a jungle temple, is an above ground structure found in jungle biomes built mostly of cobblestone and mossy cobblestone. The jungle pyramid contains two loot chests, one at the end of a hallway of arrow booby traps, and one hidden behind a lever puzzle.
entities.name: Jungle Pyramid

entities.blurb: A woodland mansion is a massive procedurally-generated structure found in dark forests and pale gardens. It is often found far away from the world spawn point. A mansion is inhabited by vindicators, evokers, and allays and is one of the only places where totems of undying can be obtained. They are primarily made of dark oak wood and cobblestone, and are filled with various rooms. Besides illagers, a mansion's interior lighting is sufficiently low for other Overworld monsters to spawn.
entities.name: Woodland Mansion

entities.blurb:
Mineshafts are common underground structures primarily found underground in the Overworld. They consist of interlinked 3×3 tunnels with incomplete rail lines running through them, with oak planks platforms bridging gaps or hanging in larger exposed caverns.
A unique variant of mineshafts made out of dark oak wood can generate on the surface in badlands biomes.
entities.name: Mineshaft

entities.blurb:
Mineshafts are common underground structures primarily found underground in the Overworld. They consist of interlinked 3×3 tunnels with incomplete rail lines running through them, with oak planks platforms bridging gaps or hanging in larger exposed caverns.

entities.name: Badlands Mineshaft

entities.blurb: A monster room, commonly known as a dungeon, is a structure-like feature found underground in the Overworld. It consists of a room with cobblestone walls and a floor made of cobblestone mixed with mossy cobblestone. A monster spawner that produces either zombies, skeletons, or spiders is found in the middle.
entities.name: Monster Room

entities.blurb: Ocean monuments, also known as simply monuments, are rare underwater structures found in deep ocean biomes and variants. They are inhabited by guardians and elder guardians. They are the only place where sponges can be found and one of the two places where prismarine can be found; the other being cold ocean ruins.
entities.name: Ocean Monument

entities.blurb: Nether fossils are fossils that generate in soul sand valleys that can sometimes contain dried ghasts.
entities.name: Nether Fossil

entities.blurb: Cold ocean ruins are variants of ocean ruins. They are underwater structures primarily composed of stone bricks. They are found in ocean biomes and rarely on beaches, and are inhabited by drowned and sometimes zombie nautiluses alongside them. They contain chests and suspicious gravel that contain a variety of loot, most notably buried treasure maps, exclusive pottery sherds, nautilus armor, and emeralds.
entities.name: Cold Ocean Ruin

entities.blurb: Warm ocean ruins are variants of ocean ruins. They are underwater structures primarily composed of sandstone. They are found in ocean biomes and rarely on beaches, and are inhabited by drowned and sometimes zombie nautiluses alongside them. They contain chests and suspicious sand that contain a variety of loot, most notably buried treasure maps, exclusive pottery sherds, nautilus armor, emeralds, and sniffer eggs.
entities.name: Warm Ocean Ruin

entities.blurb: A pillager outpost is an assortment of generated structures inhabited by pillagers. Pillager outposts are one of the most reliable ways to find raid captains, who can be killed to obtain ominous bottles, which can then be used to start raids and increase the difficulty of trial chambers.
entities.name: Pillager Outpost

entities.blurb: A ruined portal is a structure resembling a damaged Nether portal, which generates commonly in both the Nether and the Overworld. It contains some decoration and a loot chest around it.
entities.name: Ruined Portal

entities.blurb: A shipwreck is a common structure found in oceanic biomes and rarely on beaches that resembles a sunken sailing ship. It contains up to three chests each with a different loot table, which can contain suspicious stew, fishing rods, and buried treasure maps, which lead to a buried treasure.
entities.name: Shipwreck

entities.blurb: A shipwreck is a common structure found in oceanic biomes and rarely on beaches that resembles a sunken sailing ship. It contains up to three chests each with a different loot table, which can contain suspicious stew, fishing rods, and buried treasure maps, which lead to a buried treasure.
entities.name: Beached Shipwreck

entities.blurb: A stronghold is an underground structure in the Overworld, and is the only place where an End portal can be found. Strongholds can be located by using an eye of ender.
entities.name: Stronghold

entities.blurb: Swamp huts (also known as witch huts) are small above ground structures where witches and black cats can spawn.
entities.name: Swamp Hut

entities.blurb: Trail ruins are buried structures that work as archaeological sites where suspicious gravel generates. They are found in heavily forested biomes and resemble ruined villages from a lost culture.
entities.name: Trail Ruins

entities.blurb:
Trial chambers are uncommon underground structures that serve as a mid-game combat challenge. They consist mostly of copper blocks and tuff bricks, and are the only place where trial spawners and vaults naturally generate. Trial chambers are also the only place where breezes spawn, whose breeze rods can be used to craft wind charges. Various materials such as heavy cores and certain armor trims are obtained exclusively by unlocking vaults in trial chambers. As it is the only source of breeze rods and heavy cores, the structure is also the only location where maces can be obtained.
Trial chambers can also be used to obtain copper bulbs without entering the Nether, and large quantities of copper blocks and their derivatives.
Most copper blocks found in trial chambers are waxed, preventing them from oxidizing. However, some unwaxed copper blocks can also generate due to a bug.
Ominous trials can also take place here through the Bad Omen effect. Bad Omen converts to Trial Omen, which causes all trial spawners to become ominous, making them more difficult and providing greater rewards.
entities.name: Trial Chambers

entities.blurb:
A village is a group or complex of buildings and other above ground structures that generate naturally in the Overworld. A village is inhabited by villagers, cats, iron golems and livestock mobs. Wandering traders with their trader llamas can occasionally spawn there.
Villages are a source of resources for the player, obtained through trading, loot chests, and other materials found within the village. They are also targeted by illager raids, which are triggered when a player with the Bad Omen effect enters a village.
entities.name: Desert Village
